newsitem.title: UK: S&N calls for 3.50-3.70 stg minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: S&N calls for 3.50-3.70 stg minimum wage.

text.p: Britain's largest brewer Scottish & Newcastle Plc hopes the new Labour government will set a minimum wage of between 3.50 and 3.70 stg an hour, chief executive Brian Stewart told reporters on Monday.
"Between the 3.50 and 3.70 level should not be too detrimental and I hope also it gives due credit to training."
"If it is up in the 4.0 pound region it will slow down investment in the pub business and that is counterproductive to job creation," he added.
The Labour government plans to introduce a minimum wage after hearing recommendations from a new Low Pay Commission made up of business and trade union representatives.

Large leisure and retail companies like Whitbread Plc and Bass Plc employ many low paid part-time bar and catering staff making their finances especially vulnerable to the introduction of a minimum wage.

So far, Labour politicians have given no indication of what they consider an appropriate level, although British Prime Minister Tony Blair said earlier this month he believed it is wrong 800,000 people in the country should earn less than 2.50 pounds an hour.
